Meta.title: Who to Attack
Meta.description: NFL coach companion: find the receivers a defense cannot keep covered (Separation Over Expected).

Shell.searchHint: Search for a player or a page

soe.name: SOE
soe.help: Separation Over Expected: yards between the receiver and the nearest defender at the throw, minus the typical value for that position, alignment and coverage. Positive = more open than expected.

epa.name: EPA
epa.help: Expected Points Added: points the play added for the offense. Higher is better for the offense.

toe.name: TOE
toe.help: Targets Over Expected: actual targets minus the targets expected from the space the player created. Negative = thrown to less than the space suggests.

rank.name: Rank
rank.help: Rank by space conceded: 1 = concedes the least space, 32 = concedes the most.

soe_allowed.name: Space conceded
soe_allowed.help: Average SOE of receivers against this defense, compared with the league average. Positive = concedes more space than average.

epa_allowed.name: EPA allowed
epa_allowed.help: Expected points per pass allowed, compared with the league average. Positive = worse for the defense.

routes.name: Routes
routes.help: Pass routes run by the player in the analyzed plays.

targets.name: Targets
targets.help: Times the quarterback threw to the player.

air_yards.name: Air yards
air_yards.help: Average distance the ball traveled in the air, per target.

cpoe.name: CPOE
cpoe.help: Completion Percentage Over Expected: how much more (or less) often passes to him are completed than a typical pass would be.

Overview.title: Who to attack
Overview.soeText: Separation Over Expected is the space a receiver had from the nearest defender at the throw, compared with what is typical for that position and coverage. Use it to pick matchups.
Overview.moversDesc: Players who created the most space above expectation, by coverage type.

quick.gameplan: Pick a matchup and get the receivers to target.
quick.replays: Watch the space on real plays.

Proof.claim: Against man coverage, throwing to an open receiver is worth about {delta} more points per pass than throwing to a covered one.
Proof.claimSub: Same pattern for completions: a receiver who gets more open than expected catches the ball more often.
Proof.epaExplain: expected points added by the play: the higher, the better for the offense.
Proof.caution: Correlation, not causation. Based on {n} targeted passes from weeks {from}–{to} of 2021; better-covered throws are also harder throws.

Coverage.manExplain: Man: each defender follows one receiver.
Coverage.zoneExplain: Zone: each defender guards an area of the field (here, "Zone" also includes other coverages).

Watch.title: Open but rarely targeted
Watch.intro: Receivers who regularly get space, yet are thrown to less often than their situations would suggest.
Watch.how: Expected targets = how often a route with this much space, this position and this coverage type is typically targeted; we compare it with the real count.
Watch.caution: These players' targets do not earn more points than others ({a} EPA per target vs {b}), and the quarterback may have good reasons not to throw to them. Examine the film before acting.

Method.title: Method & limits

soe.name: SOE: Separation Over Expected
soe.text: Yards between the receiver and the nearest coverage defender at the throw, minus the median for the same position, alignment group and coverage type. Player averages are shrunk toward zero when samples are small.

epa.name: EPA: Expected Points Added
epa.text: How many points the play added for the offense, from nflverse play-by-play. Higher is better for the offense.

toe.name: TOE: Targets Over Expected
toe.text: Actual targets minus expected targets, where expected = how often a route with that much space, position and coverage type is typically targeted.

cover.name: Man vs Zone
cover.text: Man: each defender follows one receiver. Zone: each defender guards an area of the field. In this app, "Zone" also includes other coverages (prevent, red zone…), so Zone share = 100% minus Man.

Method.b1: Data: 2021 season, weeks 1–8 only, {plays} passing plays. Penalties, sacks, scrambles and plays without a throw are excluded.
Method.b2: Small samples, especially against man coverage: individual numbers are shrunk toward zero and labeled when the sample is small.
Method.b3: SOE measures space at the moment of the throw, not route quality, speed or the quarterback's accuracy.
Method.b4: Targeted receivers and expected points (EPA) come from nflverse public play-by-play, joined exactly to the tracking plays: {n} targeted passes.
Method.b6: "Zone" includes the other coverages (e.g. prevent, red zone), so Zone share = 100% minus Man. Team SOE averages are raw (not centered), so teams are always compared with the league average.
Method.b5: Replays are the best cases, selected to illustrate. Completion rates and EPA show correlations, not proven causes.
Method.foot: Data: NFL Big Data Bowl tracking · nflverse · Built for the AWS x NFL hackathon
Method.intro: Understand the metrics and data scope behind each analysis.

Radar.title: NFL Optimal Target & Mismatch Radar
Radar.pitch: For the offensive coordinator: on passing downs, which receiver was the best option and did the QB find him? Metric:
Radar.otsDef: OTS (0-99) combines current separation and projected separation at +0.5 s, x1.25 for a mismatch (RB/TE on a linebacker, or a speed edge above 1.5 yd/s) and x1.20 if the receiver gets past the first-down line.
Radar.kpiGainHelp: Extra projected yards of separation for RB/TE covered by a linebacker vs other cases.
Radar.kpiIgnore: EPA per pass when the QB finds the most open option vs otherwise
Radar.kpiIgnoreHelp: The QB skips the most open option on {pct}% of plays, but a random pick would give {baseline}%: the baseline matters. What counts is EPA per pass.
Radar.kpiOtsHelp: Average Optimal Target Score on mismatch routes vs all other routes.
Radar.honesty: Honesty note: with about 5 eligible receivers, a QB would miss the top-OTS one around 80% of the time by pure chance, so compare the skip rate to that baseline. OTS is a model, not an absolute truth; the QB also sees coverage, pressure and timing. Small samples: always check n.
Radar.lbDesc: Receivers who are often the best option but get targeted less than expected.
Radar.minMismatch: At least 5 mismatch routes and 10 routes; sorted by mismatch win rate by default.
Radar.bestVsActualTitle: Best target {best}% of the time, actually targeted {actual}%
Radar.fieldDesc: Pick a featured play and scrub through it. Dotted line: receiver to his nearest defender.
Radar.qbGap: {n, plural, =0 {QB found the best} other {QB gap: # OTS}}
Radar.insightNone: No eligible target identified on this play.
Radar.insightFound: {down, selectordinal, one {#st} two {#nd} few {#rd} other {#th}} & {ytg} ({cov}): the QB found the best target, his {bestPos} (OTS {bestOts}){mm, select, yes {, a mismatch against {def} with {sep} yds of projected separation} other { with {sep} yds of projected separation}}.
Radar.insightMiss: {down, selectordinal, one {#st} two {#nd} few {#rd} other {#th}} & {ytg} ({cov}): the QB targets his {tgtPos} (OTS {tgtOts}) while his {bestPos} is {mm, select, yes {in a mismatch against {def} with {sep} yds of projected separation (OTS {bestOts})} other {more open, with {sep} yds of projected separation (OTS {bestOts})}}.
